question: According to recent analyses1, the Italian national health service shows growing regional disparities in the provision of essential levels of care (LEA), with a marked gap between northern and southern regions.

In particular, regions subject to financial recovery plans, such as Sicily, continue to face serious structural problems, staff shortages and organisational difficulties, which are undermining equitable and timely access to care. There are other alarming signs: a rise in private health expenditure, among the highest in Europe, and an increase in interregional health mobility.

This state of affairs is unfolding against a backdrop in which Italian public health expenditure accounts for some 6.4 % of GDP, below the EU average (6.9 %), and estimated real growth of about 1 %. At the same time, national recovery and resilience plan (NRRP) mission 6 (‘Health’) earmarks EUR 15.

6 billion in Recovery and Resilience Facility funding for local care, digitalisation and infrastructure, but the Court warns of implementation delays and staff shortages. In the light of Article 168 TFEU: 1.
What steps will the Commission take to monitor and combat the growing regional inequalities in access to LEA, particularly in regions subject to financial recovery plans?

With a view to delivering real progress in reducing regional health inequalities, is the Commission in favour of increased coordination, monitoring and support in the implementation of NRRP mission 6?
Report by Italy’s Court of Auditors to Parliament on the management of regional health services for the financial years 2023-24 (Decision No 21/SEZAUT/2025/FRG).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.3.2026) The Commission recognises the importance of tackling regional disparities in Italy regarding access to healthcare, and monitors these issues, especially within the framework of the European Semester.

In line with the objective of supporting access to primary healthcare services, especially in regions where access is more difficult, Mission 6 of the Italian recovery and resilience plan (NRRP)1 includes, amongst others, several measures aimed at improving territorial healthcare assistance.

In particular, it establishes a new organisational model for the territorial healthcare network and it further supports the investments needed for its full implementation. The Commission services are in constant dialogue with the Italian authorities regarding the implementation of the Italian NRRP.

While the Commission assesses the fulfilment of the milestones and targets envisaged in the Council Implementing Decision (CID) for the Italian NRRP and ensures coordination, monitoring, and support in implementing its measures, the national authorities remain primarily responsible for implementing their Plan as detailed in the CID Annex.
1 Annex to the Council Implementing Decision amending Implementing Decision of 13 July 2021 on the
approval of the assessment of the recovery and resilience plan for Italy, https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15106-2025-ADD-1/en/pdf.
